message:
Thanks. Based on what you've shared (two children, household income about $139,800 from work), most income-based programs look out of reach. I need three more details to confirm:
1. Is there a married couple in the household?
2. Does anyone get health insurance through a job?
3. How many people live in your household, including you? (I'm assuming 4.)
reply: I don't really know. I don't really know. Four of us.

summary: Household of 4 (two adults in their thirties, two children) with about $139,800 in annual work income. None of the ten programmes look likely to apply. SNAP, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, school meals and WIC are all income-tested well below this level (WIC and school meals also have no eligible child or pregnancy for WIC as far as we know; the household is far above income limits regardless). ACA premium tax credit is out because income is above the subsidy limit for a family of 4 and, if anyone has job-based insurance, that also rules it out. Child tax credit: the full credit is not limited at this income, but the refundable part only pays out when tax owed is lower than the credit, which is unlikely at this income, so no refundable payment is expected. Not confirmed: marital status and whether job-based health insurance is offered; neither changes the result above. If the household's income or family situation is different from what was described (for example, income falling sharply during the year or a change in household size), rerun the screening.
